landing.flashcard_spiegate_da_un_tutor: Flashcards explained by an AI tutor with a real voice, adapting to whatever you are studying.
landing.qual_e_il_present_perfect: What is the present perfect of
landing.blue_have_has_bold_gone: /blue{Have/Has} + /bold{gone}. Used for a past action with an effect that still matters now.
landing.le_flashcard_lo_sfruttano: Flashcards turn that to your advantage.
landing.nel_1885_lo_psicologo_hermann: In 1885 the psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus described the "forgetting curve": without review, most of what we learn slips away within days.
landing.ascoltare_una_spiegazione_senza_fermarti: Listening to an explanation without stopping to repeat it
landing.sensazione_di_sapere_che_dura: A feeling of knowing — that fades fast
landing.rispondere_prima_di_guardare_la: Answering before looking at the solution
landing.spiegarlo_ad_alta_voce_con: Saying it out loud, in your own words
landing.rivedere_la_scheda_proprio_quando: Revisiting the card right when you were about to forget it
landing.non_e_una_sensazione_e: This is not a feeling. It is measured.
landing.negli_ultimi_cinquant_anni_la: Over the past fifty years cognitive psychology has compared study methods in controlled experiments. The results agree.
landing.nell_esperimento_di_roediger_e: In Roediger and Karpicke's experiment, those who had only reread the material forgot far more than those who had tested themselves.
landing.a_parita_di_tempo: For the same amount of time
landing.la_ricerca_sulla_pratica_dilazionata: Research on spaced practice shows the advantage grows the longer the gap between the study session and the exam.
landing.tutto_quello_che_serve_per: Everything you need to study actively, without the hassle.
landing.copi_un_prompt_gia_pronto: Copy a ready-made prompt, paste it into ChatGPT or Gemini, check the result and save it. Or write your cards by hand.
landing.poca_energia_o_poco_tempo: Low on energy or time for a long explanation? "Break it up" turns one card into several micro-questions.
landing.ogni_scheda_puo_essere_spiegata: Every card can be explained out loud, with metaphors generated for that specific card.
landing.un_pulsante_un_esempio_pratico: One button, one worked example tailored to that card: for when theory alone is not enough.
landing.ripassa_parlando_senza_toccare_lo: Review by talking, without touching the screen: perfect in the car or on a walk.
landing.streak_obiettivo_giornaliero_traguardi_s: Streak, daily goal, unlocked milestones and how your accuracy moves over time.
landing.pronto_a_ricordare_invece_che: Ready to remember instead of reread?
landing.impara_l_inglese_e_tutto: — learn English, and everything else, and actually remember it.
landing.studio_roediger: In a study by Roediger and Karpicke, those who only {rileggere} the material had forgotten {perso1} of what they knew two days later. Those who {testato} had lost just {perso2}.
landing.dunlosky: Of 10 common study techniques reviewed by Dunlosky and colleagues (2013), only two earned a "high utility" rating: {richiamo} (flashcards) and {pratica} over time. Rereading, highlighting and summarising — the techniques students use most — came out among the least effective.
landing.fonti: Sources: Dunlosky et al., {r1} (2013) · Roediger & Karpicke, {r2} (2006) · retrievalpractice.org

import.spiegazione:
A sheet with a Habit column can hold many of them; otherwise each sheet is one habit and its name becomes the title. The check-in dates are needed, and ideally the time.
I recognise the columns by name: if I get it wrong, you can fix it after the upload.

fc.ibf_prompt_base:
I am using a personal flashcard site. I would like you to generate flashcards on the topic: [PUT THE TOPIC HERE]
Using EXACTLY the following formatting rules of the site:
1. TEXT: You can start a new line whenever you like to make it easier to read. Use these commands to highlight the important parts:
  to colour the text: /red{testo}, /blue{testo}, /green{testo}, /purple{testo}, /orange{testo}, /gray{testo}.
  to highlight the text: /yellow{testo}.
  to format it: for important things: /bold{testo}, /underline{testo}. for additions or examples: /italic{testo}.
2. LISTS: Used for bullet points. You can choose the colour of the side bar with: /list-red{}, /list-blue{}, /list-green{}, /list-purple{}, /list-orange{}, /list-gray{} (or simply /list{} for the default colour).
  Bullet points follow these rules:
  - Use leading dashes for the levels ("-" level 1, "--" level 2, "---" level 3 and so on, no limit).
  - To start a new line inside a bullet point without creating a new bullet, go to a new line and write the text without a dash.
  This is an example of a formatted list:
/list-blue{
  - first main point
  - second main point
  text that continues on a new line inside the second point without making a new bullet
  -- first sub-point of the second point
  --- first sub-sub-point
  - third main point}
3. LATEX FORMULAS: Inline LaTeX goes between $ $ (e.g. the formula is $ formula $, and so on). Displayed LaTeX on its own line goes between $$ $$ (e.g. the formula is $$ formula $$ and so on). CAREFUL: never put a full stop or a comma straight after the double dollar, or you will get a line with a single full stop! Wrong: $$ formula $$, and so on.
